report.title: 2025 Consumer Confidence Report - Chemeketa Park MWC

sources_described: Surface water from Moody Gulch Creek (source 002_002; intake at the north entrance of Ogallala Warpath at Old Santa Cruz Hwy), treated by conventional surface water treatment. The company website adds that treated water from San Jose Water's Montevina Pipeline is a secondary source used only in emergencies.

violations: Lead Action Level Exceedance (Table 7, page 12): 'During September 2025, Chemeketa Park MWC collected 5 lead tap samples. One sample at 17708 Blackfoot Trail (9/24/2025) returned 36.4 µg/L, resulting in a 90th percentile of 18.2 µg/L, which exceeds the lead action level of 15 µg/L. A Tier 1 Public Notice was distributed to all customers on 11/19/2025. Follow-up samples collected on 11/25/2025 at the original exceedance site and the Tank Outlet (distribution system entry point) both returned 0.1 µg/L, well below the action level, indicating the exceedance was isolated to premise plumbing at one address and not systemic.' Duration: September-October 2025 monitoring period; continuing corrosion control evaluation and enhanced lead monitoring.

HAA5 MCL Violation (Table 7, page 13): 'On 11/19/2025, an HAA5 sample at 20891 Comanche Trail returned 195 µg/L (0.195 mg/L), exceeding the MCL of 60 µg/L (0.060 mg/L). A Citation and Compliance Order (No. 02_17_26J_005) was issued by the Division of Drinking Water on March 18, 2026.' Causes: naturally occurring organic matter (tannins) in the Moody Gulch source, elevated sodium hypochlorite dosage to maintain CT disinfection in cold weather, and increased water age at Comanche Trail. Duration November 2025 - ongoing; Tier 2 public notification; quarterly monitoring; Corrective Action Plan submitted June 2026; new 82,286-gallon contact-time tank installed April 2026; distribution flushing bi-weekly from April 2026, weekly from May 2026. Trend: 195 µg/L (Nov 2025), 102 µg/L (Feb 2026), 72 µg/L (May 2026).

TTHM MCL Violation (Table 7, page 14): 'On 11/19/2025, a TTHM sample at 20891 Comanche Trail returned 160 µg/L (0.160 mg/L), exceeding the MCL of 80 µg/L (0.080 mg/L).' Same causes and corrective actions as HAA5; duration November 2025 - ongoing. Trend: 160 µg/L (Nov 2025), 85 µg/L (Feb 2026), 82 µg/L (May 2026). 'Chemeketa Park MWC expects to return to full compliance by December 31, 2026.'
extraction_notes: State SWS CCR template prepared by Cypress Water Services; the PDF's internal 'file' page count says 8 but pypdf and the printed footers give 15 pages, and 1-based page numbers follow the footers. Asterisked results (lead 90th percentile 18.2 ppb, HAA5 195 ppb, TTHM 160 ppb) are MCL/AL exceedances detailed in Table 7 (pages 12-14). HAA5 and TTHM are single 11/19/2025 results (no running annual average printed). Aluminum appears in both the primary (MCL 1) and secondary (SMCL 0.2) tables and is recorded twice. Secondary-table turbidity unit is printed 'units'. Table 6 (unregulated) is 'None'; Table 11 (surface water TT violations) is 'None'. Table 8/9 (groundwater) are not present in this report.
